qs.q: A 67-year-old man undergoes a standard transurethral resection of the prostate for an 85-gram gland. Which surgical approach would provide a lower re-operation rate for a prostate of this size?
qs.e: Open prostatectomy is indicated for very large glands over 75 to 80 grams and offers a lower re-operation rate than TURP. Transurethral incision is restricted to small glands under 30 grams.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: A 64-year-old man undergoes transurethral resection of the prostate and later notices cloudy, painful urination along with fever. What is the most appropriate management step to establish a diagnosis?
qs.e: Fever or painful urination post-TURP indicates a potential infection and requires a urine culture. Routine alpha-blockers will not address a suspected postoperative urinary tract infection.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: A 72-year-old man develops acute confusion, nausea, and initial hypertension followed by hypotension during a prolonged transurethral resection of the prostate. What is the most immediate pharmacological treatment for the suspected underlying fluid complication?
qs.e: TURP syndrome is treated by stopping the operation, giving oxygen, and administering furosemide along with cautious hypertonic saline for severe hyponatraemia. Normal saline would worsen the dilutional hyponatraemia.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: A 66-year-old man is counselled regarding common long-term sexual complications following a successful transurethral resection of the prostate. What is the approximate expected incidence of retrograde ejaculation?
qs.e: Retrograde ejaculation occurs in about 65% of patients after TURP, whereas erectile dysfunction affects up to 14%. Incontinence occurs in less than 10% of cases.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: During a transurethral resection of the prostate, hypotonic irrigation fluid is absorbed through opened venous sinuses. Which laboratory abnormality is characteristic of this complication?
qs.e: Absorption of hypotonic irrigation fluid leads directly to dilutional hyponatraemia and hypervolaemia. Hypernatraemia is incorrect as the absorbed fluid lacks sodium.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: A 74-year-old man receives postoperative instructions following a transurethral resection of the prostate. For how many weeks should he be advised to avoid heavy lifting, driving, and sexual activity?
qs.e: Post-operative advice includes avoiding heavy lifting, driving, and sex for about 2 weeks, while urgency and frequency settle by about 6 weeks. Blood in the urine can also be expected for about 2 weeks.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs

qs.q: A 71-year-old man is recovering in the ward after a transurethral resection of the prostate where a three-way catheter with continuous bladder irrigation was placed. For how many days is this catheter typically maintained?
qs.e: A three-way catheter with continuous bladder irrigation is left for 1 to 3 days following a TURP procedure. Leaving it for weeks increases infection risk without added benefit.
qs.s: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) and Acute Urinary Retention: MCQs
